angle: RISK-FIRST: the tabless editor frame and its single dock go first (they break the most tests and every later editor batch mounts into them), then the start-up byte budget (Documents), then the render-count-pinned editor forms, the parity-walker-pinned Design drawer, the remaining editor tools, the workspace shell that Applications and Projects depend on, Applications, and last the largest but lowest-risk Projects area; a final integration batch sweeps phones, parked items and the full gate. 14 batches, about 41 hours of work, about 16 five-hour cycles with spill.
principles: Order by risk, not by screen: (1) tabless editor + dock + tab-test rewrite, (2) start-up path at about 0 kB spare, (3) render-count tests 165/173 and resume-tab.mjs (112 files), (4) parity walker and apply-on-click, (5) workspace shell + routes, (6) the job drawer and its Back behaviour, (7) the big lazy but low-risk Projects area. Low-risk restyles come last.

Parity file first, board second: where a board and a parity row disagree the parity Fix column wins, and where the audit cannot tell, the live app wins (PARITY-RULE). Each batch brief B<n>.md carries a 'board says X, build Y' table made verbatim from the batch's CHANGED and MISSING rows, so no builder is shown a function-dropping design without the correction next to it.

Every batch starts with a no-visual-change safety-net commit (data-testid hooks on the old controls, helpers that use them) and only then swaps the markup, so the e2e and node helpers are written once and the swap changes no spec. First applied in B1 (testids on today's tab buttons, openDesign/openAts/switchTo helpers, entry-header and entry-title ids for resume-tab.mjs and 165).

Start-up ledger: only B2 and B3 (and a one-line import in AppRoutes.jsx by B2) edit start-up files. B2 reads the real margin first, buys headroom with invisible offsets (lazy NewLetterModal and its Dialog closure, lazy CareerHistoryPanel, dynamic jsonResumeImport), then allots bytes per cluster; the 71-startup-chunks diagnostic is read on CI after every start-up push. Every other batch is lazy-chunk only and never adds a module that both the Dashboard and a lazy page import (it would be hoisted into the entry).

index.css is touched by one cluster per batch and only in B1 (additive brief tokens), B2/B3 (start-up component classes cv-*, so JSX class strings stay short) and B9 (flip the kit tokens by aliasing them to the cv tokens). No other batch edits it.

Single-owner files by batch: Editor.jsx, EditorHeader.jsx, useEditorTab.js, EditorPreviewPane.jsx = B1 (B8 later edits only the EditorAlerts block of EditorHeader.jsx); DesignPanel*.jsx = B6; PersonalInfoEditor*.jsx = B5; Dashboard.jsx, AuthBar.jsx, ResumeCard.jsx = B2 then B3 in sequence; AppRoutes.jsx = B2 (PageLoading import only), B9 (shell routes), B10 (jobs lines only); parity registries = only the batch that moves or renames a control, in the same commit as the control. Inside a batch each cluster owns different files and never edits another cluster's file; a file two clusters need is given to one and the other asks the lead.

Phone is built with its desktop screen (the code is responsive), so each batch owns the MOBI rows of its screens and runs a narrow-width lens in its bug hunt; B14 sweeps 390 and 768-1099 px over every board. The editor's phone frame is part of B1 because the tab bar disappears on phones too.

Tests: every src commit has a test that fails without it, proved with failfirst on CI; stale tests are updated to the intended behaviour with the evidence in the commit message and the batch report, never weakened; a parked item gets a negative twin inside the test of the function that sits next to it (it cannot be failfirst'ed alone). Tooltip-level wording that no row lists is protected by a label diff: before and after each batch the lead diffs the title=, aria-label=, placeholder= and data-testid strings of the batch's files and every removed string must be a deliberate, recorded rename.

CI order per batch (parity/_ci.md): failfirst dispatch per src commit, then ONE targeted dispatch (tests + the batch's browser specs + 71-startup-chunks), then ONE full gate (no inputs) on the final head. Browser specs ride in the single targeted dispatch; only red files are re-run. The perf harness (perf: browser) runs once in B1 and once in B14 because only those touch the typing path.

Catch-all rules so no row falls through: every other row of editor-content.md (including any row added by review in sections 5 and 6) belongs to B4; every other row of editor-design-templates.md (including section 1B) belongs to B6; every other row of editor-letter-ats-export.md (including section 5) belongs to B5; every other row of shell-docs.md (including 1i and 1j) belongs to B3; every other row of applications.md (including section 5) belongs to B11; every other row of projects.md (including section J) belongs to B13; every other row of mobile.md (including section 6) belongs to B14. The DRAWN BUT NOT IN THE LIVE APP sections of all seven files (NEW-xxx, NEW-0x, D-xx, N1..N17 and the review additions) belong to B14: it checks each against the built UI (parked means absent, same-function-other-name means present and already pinned by its owner batch). IDs EDIT- and NEW- exist in BOTH editor-content.md and editor-design-templates.md: always read the pair as file plus ID.

Accessibility is deferred: batches keep markup semantic where it costs nothing, record any a11y gap they see in their report's 'a11y notes', and fix none (no aria, role, contrast, focus or target-size work).

Resume-ability: each batch writes batches/B<n>.md before it starts and B<n>-report.md at the end; plan-work/plan-risk.json, the briefs and RUN-STATE live in the pushed branch so a container restart costs one stage. All commits are sairamgudiputi, no trailers, branch claude/wonderful-maxwell-vu8xqw only, never master.

canvasCorrections.whenAndHow: No redraw before the build. About 430 of the roughly 1,040 rows are CHANGED or MISSING, but the 335 MISSING rows nearly all mean 'no drawn home', and their Fix column says restore or keep the live control, which the live components already render; a correction pass over 39 boards would cost about a day of drawing and review, delay Batch 1, and give the builder little it does not already have in the parity Fix column.
